quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #6
										  					
  

50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: You can cross double yellow lines to pass another vehicle if the:

options.text: Vehicle in front of you moves right to let you pass.
Yellow line on your side of the road is broken.
Yellow line on the opposite side of the road is broken.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yellow line on your side of the road is broken.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line means traffic on that side can pass if it is safe to do so.

questions.question: To stay out of a truck or bus driver's blind spot, you should:

options.text: Never pass them.
Don't drive next to them and don't follow too closely.
Flash your lights at them.
Sound your horn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Don't drive next to them and don't follow too closely.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles like trucks and buses have big blind spots on the sides and rear. Avoid driving beside them and don't tailgate them.

questions.question: A seat belt should be adjusted so that it:

options.text: Is loose.
Fits snugly across your hip bones and lower abdomen.
Is hidden under the seat.
Stops the seat belt warning light or buzzer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fits snugly across your hip bones and lower abdomen.
questions.explanation: The lap belt should fit snugly across your hip bones and lower abdomen. The shoulder belt should be comfortable with room for your fist between the belt and your chest.

questions.question: You should always drive at a speed that is:

options.text: The same as the vehicles around you.
At the speed limit.
Safe for the road and weather conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Safe for the road and weather conditions.
questions.explanation: Your speed should match road conditions, weather, and the legal speed limit. Never drive above the speed limit. Slow down when conditions are not ideal.

questions.question: Before entering a curve, you should:

options.text: Turn on your turn signal.
Slow down.
Brake hard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: You can drive slower than the speed limit for safety, but you cannot drive faster than it. Reduce speed for curves, hills with limited visibility, slippery roads, and areas with pedestrians or animals.

questions.question: Stop lines are solid white lines painted across traffic lanes at:

options.text: Curves and hills.
Churches and schools.
Intersections and pedestrian crosswalks.
Freeway on-ramps.

questions.correctAnswerText: Intersections and pedestrian crosswalks.
questions.explanation: Stop lines are solid white lines at intersections and pedestrian crosswalks. They show exactly where you must stop.

questions.question: A yellow and black diamond-shaped sign:

options.text: Warns you about conditions on or near the road.
Directs you to cities and towns ahead.
Tells you about traffic laws.
Tells you about road construction ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Warns you about conditions on or near the road.
questions.explanation: Warning signs tell you about road conditions ahead. They are usually diamond-shaped with black symbols on a yellow background.

questions.question: You are driving on a city street and see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights behind you. What should you do?

options.text: Drive to the right edge and slow down.
Drive to the right edge and stop.
Stay in your lane, slow down, and let it pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the right edge and stop.
questions.explanation: You must give the right-of-way to emergency vehicles using sirens and lights. Move to the right edge and stop until it passes. If you are in an intersection, drive through first, then stop.

questions.question: An arrow painted on the pavement means:

options.text: Drivers in that lane may make the movement shown, if they choose to.
Drivers in that lane must make the movement shown only if traffic lights are broken.
Drivers in that lane must always stop before making the movement shown.
Drivers in that lane must make the movement shown and follow traffic signal directions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers in that lane must make the movement shown and follow traffic signal directions.
questions.explanation: An arrow painted on the pavement shows drivers in that lane the movement they must make. Follow all traffic signs and signals before proceeding in the direction of the arrow.

questions.question: Should you always drive slower than other traffic?

options.text: No, driving too slowly can block traffic.
Yes, it is good defensive driving.
Yes, it is always safer than driving faster.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, driving too slowly can block traffic.
questions.explanation: Slow down when there is heavy traffic or bad weather. However, if you drive too slowly and block the normal flow of traffic, you can be cited.

questions.question: At night, to reduce headlight glare from oncoming cars, where should you look?

options.text: Straight ahead.
Over your shoulder.
At the center of the road.
To the right edge of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: To the right edge of the road.
questions.explanation: If oncoming drivers don't dim their lights, watch the right side of the road ahead. Don't look directly at the oncoming headlights. The glare can blind you for several seconds.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Side road.
Keep to the side shown by the arrow.
You may drive in the left lane.
You have the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep to the side shown by the arrow.
questions.explanation: This is a "Keep right" sign. It tells you that a traffic island, median, or barrier is ahead. You must drive to the right of it.

questions.question: When can you cross a dashed white line?

options.text: At any time.
Only during daylight hours.
When it is safe to change lanes.
Only when passing a motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: When it is safe to change lanes.
questions.explanation: Dashed white lines separate lanes going in the same direction. You may cross them to pass other vehicles if it is safe to do so.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Continue at your current speed.
You must stop ahead.
Speeding is not allowed.
There is a traffic signal ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is a traffic signal ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a traffic signal is coming up ahead.

questions.question: What must you do when you see a flashing red traffic signal?

options.text: Slow down at the light.
Drive carefully without stopping.
Merge to the right.
Stop before entering the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop before entering the intersection.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means you must stop. Yield to traffic and pedestrians. Go only when it is safe. At railroad crossings, a flashing red light means a train is coming. Wait until the lights stop flashing and all warning devices are off before you go.

questions.question: What is distracted driving?

options.text: Very uncommon.
Extremely risky behavior.
Nothing to worry about.
No more dangerous than normal driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Extremely risky behavior.
questions.explanation: Distracted driving is extremely risky. It puts you, your passengers, pedestrians, cyclists, and other drivers in danger. Paying full attention to driving helps prevent crashes.

questions.question: You are waiting in line at a stop sign. The cars ahead pass through, and there is no oncoming traffic. What must you do?

options.text: You may go through without stopping again.
You must stop again at the stop sign before going.
You may slowly roll past the stop sign.
You may follow the car ahead without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must stop again at the stop sign before going.
questions.explanation: You must always make a complete stop at a stop sign. Check for traffic before you go. Don't skip stopping just because other cars are waiting too.

questions.question: How can you prevent drowsiness on long trips?

options.text: Turn on your car radio.
Slow down.
Stop regularly to rest and stretch.
Move your eyes side to side while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop regularly to rest and stretch.
questions.explanation: On long trips, take regular breaks. Rest and stretch even if you don't feel tired. This helps prevent drowsiness.

questions.question: When merging onto an interstate highway, what should you do?

options.text: Find a safe gap and merge into traffic.
Merge across two lanes at once.
Always stop before entering the highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Find a safe gap and merge into traffic.
questions.explanation: Find a gap that is large enough for your car. Merge smoothly into the traffic flow. Do not stop on the entrance ramp unless there is no safe gap to enter.

questions.question: After passing another vehicle, when is it safe to return to your lane?

options.text: When the driver you passed signals for you to return.
After you signal for three seconds.
When you see the passed vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you see the passed vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Make sure you are far enough ahead of the car you passed. Look in your rearview mirror. When you can see both headlights of the other car, you have enough room to return to your lane safely.

questions.question: You are driving at the speed limit when the traffic light turns yellow. What should you do?

options.text: Slow down and go through the intersection without worrying.
Speed up to cross before the light turns red.
Stop before entering the intersection if you can do so safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop before entering the intersection if you can do so safely.
questions.explanation: A yellow light means the light will turn red soon. Stop if you can do so safely. If you cannot stop safely, drive through carefully.

questions.question: Even a small amount of alcohol in your blood can affect your:

options.text: Right-of-way privileges.
Judgment and physical coordination.
Knowledge.

questions.correctAnswerText: Judgment and physical coordination.
questions.explanation: Any amount of alcohol can harm your ability to drive safely. Even small amounts affect your judgment and coordination. Driving with any amount of alcohol can result in criminal charges.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Hunting area.
State park.
Deer crossing.
Wildlife preserve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Deer crossing.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that deer cross the road in this area. Slow down, stay alert, and be ready to stop.

questions.question: You stopped for a train at a railroad crossing. After the train passes, what should you do?

options.text: Wait for the signal lights to stop flashing.
Look for a second train.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: After a train passes, watch for a second train on any track. Do not move until all gates are up and all warning lights have stopped flashing.

questions.question: Which statement is correct?

options.text: Use your left foot to brake.
Use your right foot for both braking and accelerating.
Always brake suddenly to make sure you stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your right foot for both braking and accelerating.
questions.explanation: Use your right foot for both braking and accelerating. Apply the brakes gently with steady pressure so your vehicle stops slowly and smoothly.

questions.question: When you approach an intersection with a flashing red light, you must:

options.text: Stop completely, let traffic and pedestrians pass, then proceed.
Slow down and go through carefully.
Stop and stay stopped while the light is red.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, let traffic and pedestrians pass, then proceed.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works like a stop sign. Come to a complete stop, let traffic and pedestrians pass, then go when it is safe.

questions.question: You are in an accident and your vehicle is blocking traffic. What should you do?

options.text: Move your vehicle off the road if possible.
Do not move your vehicle under any circumstances.
Wait for police before moving your vehicle.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move your vehicle off the road if possible.
questions.explanation: After a minor accident, move your vehicle off the road if you can. Do not leave the scene without giving your information and helping if needed.

questions.question: Seat belts must be worn by:

options.text: Only children under 16 years old.
Only the driver.
Everyone in the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Everyone in the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Wisconsin law requires the driver and all passengers to wear seat belts while the vehicle is moving.

questions.question: This sign is a:

options.text: Service sign.
Regulatory sign.
Warning sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning sign.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. They alert you to dangers ahead, such as road changes, steep slopes, or hazards that require you to take action.

questions.question: You want to pass a pedestrian walking on the road, but a vehicle is coming toward you. What should you do?

options.text: Slow down and let the oncoming vehicle pass before you pass the pedestrian.
Keep driving at the same speed. The oncoming vehicle must stop for you.
Honk your horn to make the pedestrian move.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and let the oncoming vehicle pass before you pass the pedestrian.
questions.explanation: Handle one hazard at a time when possible. If you want to pass a pedestrian but a vehicle is coming, slow down and let the vehicle pass first. Then pass the pedestrian if it is safe.

questions.question: When must you show proof of insurance to police?

options.text: Only if you are in a crash.
If you are in a crash or stopped for a ticket.
Only if you are stopped and given a ticket.

questions.correctAnswerText: If you are in a crash or stopped for a ticket.
questions.explanation: You must carry proof of insurance whenever you drive. Show your proof of insurance and license to an officer when asked after a traffic stop or crash.

questions.question: What should you do at a flashing yellow light?

options.text: Wait for the green light.
Slow down and cross carefully.
Stop before crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and cross carefully.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down and be careful. Watch for other cars and pedestrians before crossing.

questions.question: If your turn signals break, what should you use to show you are turning?

options.text: Your horn
Your headlights
Hand signals
Your emergency flashers

questions.correctAnswerText: Hand signals
questions.explanation: If your turn signals do not work, use hand signals to show other drivers which way you are turning.

questions.question: What color and shape are construction zone signs?

options.text: Square or rectangular with white and red.
Round or octagonal with black and yellow.
Diamond-shaped or rectangular with orange and black.

questions.correctAnswerText: Diamond-shaped or rectangular with orange and black.
questions.explanation: Work zone signs have an orange background with black letters. You will see them on the right side of the road, or on both sides if the road is divided.

questions.question: What should you do at a flashing red light?

options.text: Drive through if no other cars are coming.
Keep driving because you have the right-of-way.
Stop only if a police officer is nearby.
Treat it like a stop sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Treat it like a stop sign.
questions.explanation: Flashing red lights are at dangerous intersections. Treat them the same way you treat stop signs.

questions.question: Can you drive off the road to pass another vehicle?

options.text: Yes, if the car ahead is turning left.
Yes, if there are two or more lanes in your direction.
No, never.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, never.
questions.explanation: Never drive off the paved road or onto the shoulder to pass another vehicle.

questions.question: When should you drive slower than the speed limit?

options.text: When anything makes driving conditions worse than normal.
When you see a police car.
When entering a highway with other cars.
When you are on a four-lane road.

questions.correctAnswerText: When anything makes driving conditions worse than normal.
questions.explanation: When roads are wet, slippery, or visibility is poor, drive slower than the speed limit. You can get a ticket for driving too fast for conditions, even if you are at or below the posted speed limit.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Pedestrians only.
Intersection ahead.
Hiking trails ahead.
School crossing ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: School crossing ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a school crossing is ahead.

questions.question: What must you do if a flagger is directing traffic in a construction zone?

options.text: Follow what the flagger tells you to do.
Do what other cars are doing, even if the flagger says something different.
Assume the flagger should not be there.
Follow normal traffic rules even though there is construction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow what the flagger tells you to do.
questions.explanation: Follow the directions of flaggers, signs, and police in construction zones. Not following these directions is illegal and dangerous to workers.

questions.question: What is defensive driving?

options.text: Spotting dangerous situations and acting to prevent accidents.
Getting ahead of bad drivers to protect yourself.
Following the car in front of you very closely.
Quickly changing lanes and weaving through traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Spotting dangerous situations and acting to prevent accidents.
questions.explanation: Defensive driving means you identify dangerous situations and take action before a crash happens. It helps you avoid problems caused by reckless, careless, or dangerous drivers and pedestrians.

questions.question: You need to make an emergency stop. What should you do?

options.text: Honk your horn to tell other cars you have stopped.
Get out of your vehicle once it stops.
Turn on your emergency flashers and stay in your vehicle if you can.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your emergency flashers and stay in your vehicle if you can.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle breaks down, get off the road if possible. Turn on your emergency flashers. Stay inside your vehicle to stay safe from traffic.

questions.question: To turn left from a multilane one-way street onto another one-way street, start your turn from:

options.text: Any lane, as long as it is safe.
The lane closest to the left curb.
The middle lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane closest to the left curb.
questions.explanation: When turning left from a one-way street to another one-way street, start your turn from the far left lane.

questions.question: When must you yield for emergency vehicles?

options.text: Never.
When you see flashing red or blue lights or hear a siren.
Only when other vehicles yield.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you see flashing red or blue lights or hear a siren.
questions.explanation: You must let emergency vehicles pass whenever they use flashing lights or sirens.

questions.question: When weather or light conditions require your lights on while driving, use:

options.text: Parking lights.
High beams.
Low beams.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beams.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog, snow, or rain. High beams reflect light back at you, causing glare and making it harder to see.

questions.question: When turning onto a street with multiple lanes in your direction, turn into:

options.text: The lane closest to your previous lane.
The lane marked with an arrow.
The middle lane.
Any lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane closest to your previous lane.
questions.explanation: Turn into the lane that is closest to the lane you came from. Do not change lanes while turning.

questions.question: Where is it safe to pass another vehicle?

options.text: In an intersection with no oncoming vehicles.
Wherever signs and road markings allow passing.
In a curve with no oncoming vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wherever signs and road markings allow passing.
questions.explanation: Never pass in intersections, parking lot entrances, or alleys. Do not pass where curves or hills block your view. Only pass where signs and road markings allow it and you have enough space to do so safely.

questions.question: The amount of alcohol in your blood is called:

options.text: Implied consent (IC).
Blood alcohol concentration (BAC).
Rate of alcohol consumption (RAC).

questions.correctAnswerText: Blood alcohol concentration (BAC).
questions.explanation: Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) measures the percentage of alcohol in your blood. A higher BAC means a person is more impaired.

questions.question: Why does driving at night require more caution?

options.text: Traffic moves faster at night.
There is more traffic at night.
Drivers cannot see as well at night.
Accidents happen more often at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers cannot see as well at night.
questions.explanation: At night, it is dark and drivers cannot see as well. You must use your headlights from half an hour after sunset until half an hour before sunrise, or whenever vehicles cannot be seen from 500 feet away.

questions.question: If bad weather makes it hard to see, you should:

options.text: Speed up to leave the road quickly.
Drive in the lane closest to oncoming traffic.
Stay farther behind other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay farther behind other vehicles.
questions.explanation: In darkness or poor weather, increase the distance between your vehicle and the one in front. This gives you more time to react to hazards you might not see in time.

questions.question: Remove all snow, frost, and ice from:

options.text: Just the windshield.
All windows.
Just the windshield and passenger window.

questions.correctAnswerText: All windows.
questions.explanation: You need to see clearly through all your windows before driving. Remove all snow, ice, and frost from your windows and mirrors.
